title: Animated Ads for Facebook and Instagram: Best Makers and Steps
summary: Animated ads suit explainers and product motion on Meta. Compare self-serve animation tools with done-for-you studios, then follow a five-step process.
body_markdown:
## The Brief: the self-serve option


The Brief, formerly Creatopy, is the self-serve route. Its[pricing page](https://www.thebrief.ai/pricing/) lists a plan at $29 a month billed annually, which is $348 a year, with static, animated (HTML5) and video ads resized to many formats. According to its[homepage](https://www.thebrief.ai/) , the Ad Studio imports Photoshop and Figma files, generates size and format variations automatically and animates ads. A tool like this suits a team that already has a motion designer and a storyboard, because the tool speeds up output but does not write the message. For a wider set of tools, see our[best AI video ad generators guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-ai-video-ad-generators) .


## How to make animated ads for Facebook, step by step


Follow five steps whichever maker you choose.


**1. Pick the one thing motion has to show.** Meta's[guidance on turning still image ads into video ads](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/4-ways-to-turn-still-image-ads-into-video-ads) , published in 2018, suggests adding one or two elements of motion over a few seconds, bringing the brand or key benefit to life, or using motion to demonstrate how the product works. If the motion does none of those jobs, the ad probably does not need it.


**2. Format for the placement.** Meta's[Reels ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) describes 9:16 video with sound on by default, with key messages inside the safe zone. For Facebook Feed, Meta's[video ad guide](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/video) recommends 4:5 at 1440 x 1800 pixels, and it lists captions and sound as optional but recommended. Export a vertical master and a 4:5 version from the same storyboard.


**3. Write for the first 15 seconds.** Meta's[mobile video ad guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/want-to-better-video-ads-for-mobile-well-show-you-how) asks for a message delivered in 15 seconds or less, the most captivating elements first, the brand shown early and an ad that works without sound. Captions are part of the animation, not an afterthought, because animated ads are often watched muted.


**4. Build or buy the motion.** A motion studio builds it by hand, a subscription queues it, or your team builds it in a self-serve tool. Ask every maker for the same storyboard, the same sizes and the same review step, so the prices can be compared on one brief.


**5. Test animation against a still.** Meta's[A/B testing tool](https://www.facebook.com/business/measurement/ab-testing) can test up to five ad variants with random, non-overlapping audience groups. Hold the offer, angle, landing page, audience and budget constant, and change only the execution, such as your best static ad against an animated version of it. Meta's own 2018 Create to Convert studies, which Meta reports, found that adding light motion to still ads gave a positive outcome for 69 percent of the brands studied, across 49 studies. Meta's evidence compares motion with still images, not animation with live action, and the result is not a forecast for your account, so run your own test. Our[guide to whether animated ads work on Meta](https://knowlify.com/articles/do-animated-ads-work-on-meta) covers what else Meta has measured.


## What to check on animated ads specifically


Check whether Meta is changing the ad for you. Meta's[Advantage+ creative page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/meta-advantage-plus/creative) lists image animation and video expansion among its AI enhancements, and it says some enhancements may be on by default and can be turned off at any time. An animated ad that is already moving can pick up an extra motion effect you did not design, so preview each placement and turn off enhancements that change the message or the product.


Check the file size and the final frame. Animation often ends on a logo card that sits under the placement's buttons or the caption bar, so review the export in every placement, not only the editor preview.


Check that the motion matches the claim. A product animation that shows a feature working when the real product does not work the same way creates a problem that motion does not solve. Approve the animation with the same claim review you would apply to a filmed ad.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for done-for-you animated ads on Facebook and Instagram, with a person checking every ad, but it does not build landing pages or run Google, TikTok or LinkedIn ads.
- Use animation when motion explains something a camera cannot, and keep the ad to one message.
- Export a 9:16 master and a 4:5 version, with captions, from one storyboard.
- Test animation against a still with the A/B testing tool, changing only the execution.


## FAQ


### What is the best animated ads maker?


For a finished batch made for you, Knowlify is our top pick, with 3D and stylized character animation for Facebook and Instagram and a person checking every ad. If you want to make ads yourself, a self-serve tool such as The Brief starts at $29 a month billed annually, but your team carries the storyboard, the sizes and the review. Choose by whether you need the work done or need a tool.


### How do I make animated ads for Facebook?


Pick one message that motion must show, then format the storyboard for 9:16 Reels and 4:5 Feed. Write the message to land in the first 15 seconds, add captions, and choose a maker that builds the motion from the same brief. Finally, test the animated version against your best still with the A/B testing tool.


### Are animated ads better than UGC ads?


Our sources do not show that either format wins across the board. Animation fits explanation, product motion and concepts a camera cannot film, while UGC fits a person's experience. Test both formats with the same offer, rather than assuming one is better. For the difference in production, see our[animated ads versus UGC guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/animated-ads-vs-ugc-ads) .


### Can a self-serve tool replace a motion studio?


A self-serve tool can produce many variations quickly, which helps with testing. It does not replace the storyboard, the brand review or the judgment about what motion should show. Studios such as Biddyco and Superside take on more of that work, at a different price and with different timelines.


### Do animated ads need a different disclosure?


It depends on how the animation was made. Meta's[transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) says it labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI features, and that it will begin detecting ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label in About this ad. The post does not say that detection is live yet. If any step of your animation used generative AI, plan for a label, and keep a record of how each file was made.
